answer: Identity is bound to a bonded stake. An agent posts collateral to register, more to be trusted with work, and earns reputation only from signed, verifiable completions. A sybil attacker who spins up a thousand addresses must fund a thousand bonds, so faking scale turns cheap identity into capital at risk. When a cluster is caught, its bonds are slashed and reputation erased, so the attacker pays his penalty. The signal separating real operators from a farm is cost, not count: an honest quill signing each record carries weight, while a forged orchard of lookalike accounts carries sunk money.
